source.title: One ticket to win them all: generalizing lottery ticket initializations across datasets and optimizers
source.authors: Ari S. Morcos; Hao-Nan Yu; Michela Paganini; Yuandong Tian

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether lottery-ticket initializations transfer across datasets and optimizers, reporting training outcomes for sparse models across new training configurations. It does not test the claim's training-error behavior directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy at convergence, not training classification error. Its CIFAR, optimizer-transfer, and mask comparisons do not measure whether training reaches zero or near-zero training error under the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates sparse initialization transfer using test accuracy after fixed training schedules. It does not measure training error, optimization speed, trainable depth, signal propagation, stability thresholds, or batch normalization's effects. Its initialization results therefore do not test V4 or another listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that winning tickets from sufficiently large datasets contain partly generic inductive biases and can transfer across natural-image datasets and optimizers. They acknowledge transfer gaps, fixed architecture topology, expensive ticket generation, and untested transfer across domains or tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Iterative magnitude pruning with late resetting; evaluates sparse winning-ticket initialization transfer across datasets and optimizers using test accuracy at convergence, rather than measuring training classification error from random initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer performance varies with source dataset size and number of classes, target dataset, architecture, and pruning fraction; SGD-to-Adam transfer underperforms random tickets at low pruning fractions but outperforms them at high fractions.

fits_no_version.finding: Transferred winning tickets often achieve test accuracy close to target-specific tickets; larger source datasets and more classes generally improve transfer (Sections 4.1–4.2, Figures 2–4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse winning-ticket initializations can transfer across natural-image classification datasets within a fixed architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG winning tickets transfer between SGD and Adam, although SGD-to-Adam tickets underperform random tickets at low pruning fractions and outperform them at high fractions (Section 4.3, Figure 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Winning-ticket transfer across optimizers depends on pruning fraction and transfer direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Global pruning outperforms layerwise pruning, and globally permuting random-ticket masks substantially reduces final test accuracy compared with preserving layerwise mask statistics (Figure 1; Appendix A.2, Figure A1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pruning structure contributes to sparse networks' final generalization performance.

record.problems: Results use test accuracy rather than training error. Several findings are presented in figures without numerical values in the supplied text; experiments are limited to natural-image classification and fixed network topologies.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the study's reported measures are test accuracy at convergence, so they do not bear on training classification error as named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error from random initialization, including corrupted labels and dependence on model size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention through identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, learning speed, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds, including recovery and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T3 classification to discusses/T6. Having no result rows is appropriate for these versions. Final test accuracy does not establish V1's training error or V4's learning speed and trainable depth; the introductory discussion of deep initialization methods supplies no original test of those claims.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and the effects of early stopping or regularization recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth comparisons, plain versus shortcut networks, and training error; no results test these claims.
Initialization comparisons for signal or gradient propagation, trainability, or depth.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, curvature, loss trajectories, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effect on accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup without normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The introduction discusses initialization, overparameterization, and trainable depth, but the study's experiments address winning-ticket transfer rather than any claim version.

tranche.reason: Section 4 measures test accuracy after fixed training schedules to evaluate sparse initialization transfer. It does not test the training error, local minima, depth, initialization speed, stability, or normalization effects specified by V1–V6.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion and both supplied excerpts agree with the text. Transfer is evaluated within natural-image classification with fixed architecture topology; test accuracy does not establish near-zero training error or faster optimization.
